why: DMN 1.6 Table 48: a date and time maps to "A string representation conforming to an ISO 8601 Date, Time or Date and Time combination. If the FEEL date and time contains an IANA timezone id, the ISO 8601 Date and Time is suffixed by the IANA timezone id in rectangular brackets, e.g. 2007-12-03T10:15:30+01:00[Europe/Paris]". The offset written is the zone's offset at that date and time, which has seconds in local mean time before the standard zones (Paris +00:09:21 in 1900). ISO 8601 and XML Schema Part 2 §3.2.7.3 write an offset with hours and minutes only: "The lexical representation of a timezone is a string of the form: (('+' | '-') hh ':' mm) | 'Z'". Writing the seconds is a deliberate departure from that form, as java.time's zoned text does: the offset cut to whole minutes, as it was, is the text of another instant.
